attribution.note: Marcus wrote these words himself in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The sentence joins a normative clause ('reason to research') to a firm, unhedged claim about the future ('trillions to be made'). Calling it a forecast fits the graded part, and the contract rightly leaves the normative clause unscored. The 'in the end' horizon is kept.

contract.note: On a plain reading, 'trillions' means at least about $2T of realized value from agents, cumulative or annual. That is a fair, ordinary reading of the plural. Treating it as open-ended because of 'in the end' matches his words. Excluding general AI spending is reasonable.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline ('in the end'). The packet cites no usable evidence: the Gartner pages could not be read, and the figures available were projections, not realized value. Nothing shows realized agent value of about $2T or more, and with no deadline, falling short so far is not failure. No conclusive event has occurred, so the claim stays unresolved.
